newsitem.title: TOGO: Rebel attack forced Mobutu from Zaire - Togo TV.
newsitem.headline: Rebel attack forced Mobutu from Zaire - Togo TV.

text.p: Zaire's ousted president, Mobutu Sese Seko, escaped a rebel attack on his home town of Gbadolite but came under fire as he and members of his entourage fled by cargo plane, Togolese state television reported on Sunday.

It said the plane carrying the veteran leader, who ruled Zaire for more than three decades but is now suffering from cancer, made a technical stop in Togo on Sunday before flying on, most likely to Morocco.

The report was the first suggestion that Laurent Kabila's rebels had tried to attack Gbadolite, where Mobutu had a jungle palace. He was believed to have been there since leaving his capital Kinshasa on Friday just before rebel forces marched in.
The television said a government statement quoted sources close to Mobutu for its account of the circumstances of his departure. It said rebel forces had tried to take the airport at Gbadolite.
Mystery has surrounded Mobutu's whereabouts, with a security official in Morocco saying that he arrived there on Saturday and a family friend in Paris saying he was still in Gbadolite on Sunday.
Kabila's rebels arrived in Kinshasa on Saturday, crowning their seven-month revolt with victory. Kabila proclaimed himself head of state of Zaire, which he renamed the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Togo television said members of Mobutu's entourage were already in Morocco. It was not immediately clear what Mobutu's ultimate destination would be. He has a villa in France, a long-time friend of his government.
Mobutu and Togo President Gnassingbe Eyadema have maintained close ties over the years. Both men came to power in military coups shortly after their countries gained independence.
